title: Introduce econ-navigator microbatch lanes and quant-footprint prescriptor
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Customers running mixed-tenancy workloads asked for safer, automated defaults that trade unit cost for predictable SLOs. Existing autotuners target single knobs (batch size, quant) but do not reason jointly about tenant budget constraints, multi-shape request distributions, or cache warmup behavior. This PR introduces the 'economy navigator' — a small runtime planner + CLI that (1) surfaces tenant-level unit-econ constraints, (2) selects a microbatch lane for low-latency hot paths, and (3) generates candidate quantization footprints constrained by budget and acceptable delta in quality. Motivation: reduce operator effort and avoid blunt defaults that either overspend or risk regressions when quantization is too aggressive. What this change does: - Add a new microbatch lane type (CompactMicroLane) that enforces a tight max-batch-size and short stall-window; intended for latency-sensitive, low-token requests. - Implement a quant-footprint prescriptor that takes workload heatmap + quality budget and returns 1..3 candidate quant profiles (e.g., int8-llm, int4-hybrid with kv-preserve) with estimated token-cost and simulated quality delta. - New rwctl econ simulate and rwctl econ apply commands for dry-run and controlled rollout of suggested defaults across tenants. - Integrates with telemetry: emits econ.choice.*, econ.sim.* and ties suggestions to per-route SLO and token-cost metrics to enable dashboarding and alerts. - Safe rollout: suggestions are annotated with a safety_score; the runtime will only apply profiles when safety_score >= 0.7 for automated rollouts; otherwise suggestions land in the Console as a recommendation. - Unit-econ linter for CI that runs sample traces against the prescriptor and flags >10% cost regressions for routes marked 'budget-sensitive'. Key implementation notes: - The prescriptor is implemented under pkg/quant/prescriptor.go and uses a small heuristic solver that models cache-hit amplification and batch shaping. - Micro-lane is implemented under pkg/batcher/micro_lane.go and plugged into the dispatcher with a new lane selector that prefers CompactMicroLane for requests matching route_annotations: { "micro_latency": true }. - CLI changes under cmd/rwctl/econ.go with a dry-run mode that emits a JSON report and a human-readable suggestion table. - Telemetry hooks: telemetry/econ.go and metrics/registry additions. Testing: - Unit tests for prescriptor heuristics and microlane behavior (pkg/quant/*_test.go, pkg/batcher/*_test.go). - Integration in the e2e perf suite with synthetic mixed-shape workload to estimate cost delta and latency tails. - Manual validation against customer traces supplied in ENG-4789 (sanitized). Rollout plan: merged to main, gated by a feature flag fleet.econ.navigator. Fleet enablement will be gradual: first internal canary, then opt-in tenants, then automated suggestions for eligible tenants. Backout path: rwctl econ rollback and runtime checks will revert to previous quant profiles if latency or quality regress above configured thresholds. Related: builds on research prototypes from ENG-4920. Impact: provides automated, conservative defaults that lower unit costs for many mixed workloads while keeping safety gates to prevent user-visible regressions.

release_notes: Adds the 'economy navigator' feature: a conservative suggestion engine that proposes microbatch lanes and constrained quant profiles per-tenant. Includes rwctl econ CLI for dry-run and apply, telemetry for tracking suggestions, and CI linter to catch large cost regressions. Feature gated behind fleet.econ.navigator.
